newsitem.title: USA: Zeigler recalling workers to reopen mine.
newsitem.headline: Zeigler recalling workers to reopen mine.

text.p: Old Ben Coal Co., a subsidiary of Zeigler Coal Holding Co., said Friday it was recalling 70 workers to a mine in Coulterville, Ill., as of Oct. 1 to prepare for its reopening in 1997.
Old Ben also said it expects to close its coal mine in Sparta, Ill., which opened in 1951, at the end of the year, affecting 190 employees there.
Mark Cavinder, vice president of Old Ben, said the company expects more than 200 employees to be recalled for the January reopening of the Zeigler #11 mine in Coulterville.
The mine, idled in 1995, first opened in 1977. It has a long-term reserve base with a potential of 10 years of productive mining, Cavinder said.
The mine in Sparta will produce 2.3 million tons of coal in 1996 and currently is the oldest operating underground mine in the state, the company said.
The Zeigler family of companies is among the nation's largest coal producers.
Zeigler's stock fell 25 cents to $17.375 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
